The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
// Transactions were being looked up without the readLock
journalLock.readLock().lock();
```
Reason:
The absence of a read lock when looking up transactions allowed concurrent access to the journal, leading to inconsistencies and missing records during the compaction process. Without proper locking, multiple threads could read and write to the journal simultaneously, causing data corruption.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
journalLock.readLock().lock();
```
Reason:
By introducing the read lock before accessing the journal, the code ensures that only one thread can read the transactions at a time, preventing concurrent modifications that could lead to missing records. This locking mechanism maintains data integrity during read and write operations.
